title: Ads, landing pages and testing
subtitle: Find ad angles, fix your landing page and test one thing at a time.
intro: In advertising, most money is lost by guessing. Claude helps you come up with varied angles, write variations, audit your landing page like a visitor in a hurry and frame clear test hypotheses. The decisions come from your real results, not from gut feelings.

steps.d: Start from a customer problem, desire or objection, then turn each angle into several hooks.
The landing page repeats the ad's exact promise, with one goal and one button.
Frame each test like this: if I change X to Y, this metric will move, because I observed Z.
Change one variable at a time, wait for enough data, then write down the result and what you learned.

prompts.title: The ad angle matrix
prompts.use: Before you build a new campaign.
prompts.prompt: You are a paid advertising strategist. Product: [PRODUCT]. Audience: [TARGET AUDIENCE]. Main objections: [OBJECTIONS]. Platform: [META, LINKEDIN, GOOGLE...]. Suggest 8 different ad angles: pain, gain, proof, comparison, objection handled, behind the scenes, real urgency, identity. Present them in a table: angle, hook of 10 words max, 40-word primary text, visual idea, the audience it speaks to best. Don't use any number or testimonial I haven't given you.

prompts.title: Variations for a creative test
prompts.use: When an ad is running and you want to know what would make it work better.
prompts.prompt: Here is my current ad: [AD TEXT AND VISUAL DESCRIPTION]. I want to test only one variable: [HOOK, VISUAL, CALL TO ACTION OR OFFER]. Write 4 variations that change only that variable, with everything else identical. For each variation, state the hypothesis being tested in one sentence. Then add an empty tracking table with these columns: variation, spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, cost per conversion, decision.

prompts.title: The landing page audit
prompts.use: When people click your ad but don't take action on the page.
prompts.prompt: Act as a visitor from my audience [TARGET AUDIENCE] arriving from this ad: [AD TEXT]. Here is my landing page: [SCREENSHOT OR PAGE TEXT]. First, describe what you understand in 5 seconds, then what makes you hesitate. Then audit the page on 6 points: match with the ad, clarity of the promise, proof, objections, call to action, mobile readability. End with a table: problem, suggested fix, priority (high, medium, low).

prompts.title: A/B test hypotheses
prompts.use: To decide what to test first on a page or a campaign.
prompts.prompt: I want to improve the conversion rate of [PAGE OR CAMPAIGN]. Before suggesting tests, ask me 5 questions about my traffic, my current numbers and what my customers say. Wait for my answers. Then suggest 5 hypotheses in this format: “If I change [X] to [Y], then [METRIC] will move, because [OBSERVATION]”. Rank them in a table with possible impact, effort and the traffic needed to reach a conclusion. Tell me which one to launch first and why.

workflow.title: Workflow: from ad angle to A/B test
workflow.where: A Claude chat with screenshots and a CSV
steps: Run the angle matrix and keep the 3 angles closest to what your customers actually say.
Have Claude audit your landing page from a mobile screenshot and fix the high priorities first.
Write the test hypothesis, then generate variations that change only one variable.
Launch the test in your ad platform with the same budget for each variation.
At the end, attach the CSV export of the results and ask Claude what they really let you conclude.

checklist: The ad's promise and the landing page headline say the same thing.
The page has one goal and a button visible on mobile without scrolling.
Each test changes only one variable at a time.
The hypothesis is written before launch, with the metric to track.
No number, review or client logo is shown without real proof.
The test runs long enough that you don't decide based on a few clicks.
mistake: Common mistake: stopping a test after two days because one variation seems to be winning. With too little data, you decide at random and think you learned something.
tip: Dr. Firas's tip: keep a test log in a spreadsheet: hypothesis, dates, result, lesson. Add it to your Claude Project so it never suggests a test you've already run.
